rows.label: Do Not Disturb
rows.help: Stays on screen, silences sounds, stops initiating actions.
rows.disclosure: Do Not Disturb leaves the buddy visible but quiet: proposals are refused and unprompted dialogue is not spoken. Poke, Grab, and Throw still work. The Cue (visual + sound) acknowledges each interaction. This switch silences the sound and keeps the visual.

rows.label: Sound
rows.help: Off silences audio cues.
rows.disclosure: A synthesized sound accompanies each Cue. This switch silences them. Do Not Disturb (above) takes the sound with it.

rows.label: Go away
rows.help: Go off screen. But still exist.

rows.label: Hide in fullscreen apps
rows.help: Steps aside for fullscreen apps.

rows.label: Appear in screenshots and screen shares
rows.help: Checked: visible in captures. Unchecked: excluded. Needs restart.

rows.label: Hide/Show Toggle
rows.help: Hides or shows from any app.

rows.label: Launch at login (unimplemented)
rows.help: Not available yet.
The character your buddy wears.
rows.disclosure: Characters are packages: art, personality, and behaviors bundled together. Two ship with the app.

rows.help: Buddies on screen now.
rows.disclosure: An Instance is one spawned buddy: a Character plus a user-given name and a stable id. Instances share Memory, and differ in personality (Instance Prompt) and behavior, never in what they know.

rows.help: Adds another buddy.

sections.heading: AI

rows.label: AI on
rows.help: Lets the model pick what happens next.
rows.disclosure: With this off, the buddy runs on static weights: predefined behaviors chosen by their declared weights, no model involved. With it on and no Harness attached, the HTTP endpoint (base URL, model, and key below) proposes behaviors and short lines. With it on and a Harness attached that answers, that Harness is the "AI brain" for every Instance.

rows.label: Ambient session wakes
rows.help: Acts on its own, not only when asked.
rows.disclosure: Ambient wakes are proactive model calls: the buddy addresses you after being idle long enough, on an exponential backoff. With this off, wakes are reactive only — you have to address it first. The switch below sets how long the first ambient wake waits.

rows.help: Throws the conversation in flight away and opens a fresh one.
rows.disclosure: Every other row stays where it is: the same AI source, the same model and key, the same Blank AI, the same Character and Instance Prompt. What goes is the conversation — the turns held here, and the history, tool results, and files the AI brain was holding for this buddy. The next wake is an opening turn rather than a follow-up. Memory is untouched.

sections.comment: Control whether the buddy improvises, and how often it starts a conversation on its own.
sections.disclosure: The buddy can run on static weights (no model calls) or with a Model API (the HTTP endpoint below, or an attached Harness). AI on with no Harness uses the HTTP endpoint. An attached Harness that answers becomes the "AI brain".

sections.heading: AI source

rows.label: AI source
rows.help: Which "AI brain" answers for the buddy.
rows.disclosure: Model API: the HTTP endpoint below. Harness · {name}: starts that Harness and makes it the AI brain. Harness · Custom: the command line below. The line below this row shows what is attached and whether it is signed in. Apply commits the pick.

rows.label: Custom command line
rows.disclosure: The command ai-buddy runs when Custom is picked above. Apply commits it and re-opens the attachment. Cancel restores the line.

rows.help: Harness signs itself in - ai-buddy never asks for credentials.
rows.disclosure: ai-buddy holds no credential for the Harness. The Harness authenticates itself, and the login command this line may show is text: nothing here runs it for you. This line shows three states: not attached, attached but not signed in (with the login command), or attached and answering (with a session UUID).

sections.comment: Choose which "AI brain" answers: Model API or an attached Harness.
sections.disclosure: Model API uses the HTTP endpoint below (base URL, model, and key). A Harness (claude, codex, cursor-agent, grok, hermes, opencode, pi, or Custom) attaches a child process and makes it the AI brain, and the HTTP rows stop driving. Apply is the one moment the attachment changes: Cancel restores both rows and leaves the running child alone.

rows.label: Harness
rows.help: Which Harness the box below is written for.
Good for this app run only: the port and the token are both new every launch, so a paste from yesterday stops connecting. Come back here and copy it again.
Paste at Hermes auth prompt; no Bearer prefix; rotates each launch.
This token reaches ai-buddy and nothing else. The Harness signs itself in.

sections.comment: For a Harness you start in your own terminal. Registering ai-buddy as an MCP server there lets it speak, move and emote the buddy on your screen. Nothing here changes which mind the Director uses.

rows.help: Fills in the Base URL below. Any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be typed there.
The endpoint and AI source rows take effect on Apply.
The last thing sent to the model.
rows.disclosure: This is the Character Prompt (opening turn) or the short follow-up (later wakes), inspectable so you can see exactly what context leaves your machine.

sections.heading: What the buddy can see

rows.label: Accessibility
rows.help: Reads the Dock's position.
rows.disclosure: Accessibility permission lets ai-buddy read the Dock's position and height, so the sprite never disappears behind it. Window metadata (bounds, owning app) requires no grant on macOS.

rows.label: Screen Recording
rows.help: Reads window titles.
rows.disclosure: Screen Recording permission lets ai-buddy read window titles. Window metadata (bounds, owning app) requires no grant on macOS, so the sprite can land on windows either way. Titles would reach MCP sensing tools; not used in v1.

rows.label: Input Monitoring
rows.help: Reacts to the mouse at once, not a second late.
rows.disclosure: Without this grant the buddy asks macOS where the cursor is on a timer, and while it sits still that timer runs once a second — so a poke, or the cursor arriving over the art, can take that long to land. With the grant, a listen-only event tap tells the buddy the moment the mouse moves or a button goes down, which is what the Linux build already gets without asking for anything. The tap's mask holds mouse events only: it cannot see the keyboard, and it modifies nothing it hears. Unchecked, the buddy goes back to the timer. macOS asks for the grant when you check the box, and the tap starts once the grant lands.

sections.comment: Checking a box asks macOS for the permission. macOS lists this app as ai-buddy, under Privacy & Security.

rows.help: One app name per line. Those windows stay out of MCP sensing.
rows.disclosure: Applications on this list never appear in MCP sensing tool results (window metadata, eventual Capture). The buddy can still sit on their windows. Password fields are excluded everywhere, regardless of this list.

sections.heading: Memory File
sections.comment: What your buddy remembers between runs.
sections.disclosure: Memory is one Markdown file, append-structured under stable headings. Shared by every Character Instance. Every recall reads the file, so an edit made outside ai-buddy is visible to the next recall. A single timestamped backup is written before a wipe.

sections.disclosure: Development switches print to stderr. Trace frames prints each frame the Engine produces. Trace hit-test prints where each click went (the sprite or click-through). Trace AI prints each model call with its context. Trace Engine prints each change of Behavior or Animation.

sections.heading: Blank AI

rows.label: Blank AI
rows.help: Built-in prompts emptied. An Instance Prompt still goes out.

sections.comment: Also for development and testing. Off is the buddy as shipped.
sections.disclosure: Blank AI empties the built-in Personality Prompt and the app-level instructions (voice rules, behavior list, reply contract). An Instance Prompt you write still goes out, so a control run can iterate a prompt under ai-buddy's conditions. The Prompt tab shows those three layers; emptied ones say Empty. Without a contract the buddy says what comes back and plays no Behavior unless that Instance Prompt asks for one. Switching it opens a new session, so no session mixes the two prompts.

sections.heading: HTTP limits

rows.label: Timeout, in seconds
rows.help: Model API hop. Expiry falls back to default behavior.

rows.label: Reply cap, in tokens
rows.help: HTTP endpoint only. Harness decides its own.
Fills in the field below. Any value the server takes can be typed there.

rows.label: Reasoning effort
rows.help: HTTP endpoint only. Sent verbatim.

sections.comment: Also for development and testing. Leave empty for the default.
sections.disclosure: Timeout is the Model API hop only: an HTTP request, then fallback to default behavior. Leave empty for 30 seconds (the default), remote or local. A Harness turn is the row under Harness attachment. Reply cap is the HTTP endpoint's alone (reply length); a Harness decides its own reply length. Reasoning effort is the HTTP endpoint's alone too, and is sent verbatim: low, medium and high are what every documented host takes, and anything else typed there is between you and your server.

sections.heading: Harness attachment

rows.label: Turn timeout, in seconds
rows.help: Harness session/prompt. Expiry cancels the turn.

rows.label: Auth retry, in seconds
rows.help: How long before retrying session/new.

rows.label: MCP server binary
rows.placeholder: beside the app, or this app as its own MCP server
rows.help: The stdio MCP server for the Harness.

rows.label: Working directory
rows.help: The directory the Harness treats as the project. Empty is the data folder. Session file and Action Log stay in the data folder.

sections.comment: Also for development and testing. Leave empty for the default.
sections.disclosure: Turn timeout: how long a session/prompt may run before session/cancel. Leave empty for 120 seconds (the default). Auth retry: how long a Harness that has not signed in is left alone before session/new is tried again. MCP server binary: the stdio MCP server handed to the Harness session. A path that is not a file falls back to the default (beside the app, or this app as its own MCP server). Working directory: the directory the Harness treats as the project. Empty is the data folder. Session file and Action Log stay in the data folder.
